audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for pool healing, Sabbath controversy, Father/Son work, life/judgment, witnesses, Scripture/Moses testimony.

verses.restored: After these things there was a feast of the Judeans, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.

familiar.text: After this there was a feast of the Jews; and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.

modern.text: Some time later there was a feast of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.

original.text: Μετὰ ταῦτα ⸀ἦν ἑορτὴ τῶν Ἰουδαίων, καὶ ⸀ἀνέβη Ἰησοῦς εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα.

verses.restored: In Jerusalem by the Sheep Gate there is a pool called in Hebrew Bethesda, having five porticoes.

familiar.text: Now there is at Jerusalem by the sheep market a pool, which is called in the Hebrew tongue Bethesda, having five porches.

modern.text: Now there is in Jerusalem near the Sheep Gate a pool with five covered colonnades, which in Hebrew is called Bethesda.

original.text: ἔστιν δὲ ἐν τοῖς Ἱεροσολύμοις ἐπὶ τῇ προβατικῇ κολυμβήθρα ἡ ἐπιλεγομένη Ἑβραϊστὶ ⸀Βηθεσδά, πέντε στοὰς ἔχουσα·

verses.restored: In these lay a multitude of those who were weak, blind, lame, and withered.

familiar.text: In these lay a great multitude of impotent folk, of blind, halt, withered, waiting for the moving of the water.

modern.text: On these walkways lay a great number of the sick, the blind, the lame, and the paralyzed.

original.text: ἐν ταύταις κατέκειτο ⸀πλῆθος τῶν ἀσθενούντων, τυφλῶν, χωλῶν, ⸀ξηρῶν.

verses.restored: [Some later manuscripts add an angel/messenger stirring the water and a healing tradition about entering first.]

familiar.text: For an angel went down at a certain season into the pool, and troubled the water: whosoever then first after the troubling of the water stepped in was made whole of whatsoever disease he had.

modern.note: The BSB follows modern critical-text practice here and does not print this traditional verse number as a separate verse.

original.note: This traditional verse number is not present as a separate verse in the SBLGNT base text; preserve as a textual-witness issue.

verses.restored: A certain human was there who had been in weakness thirty-eight years.

familiar.text: And a certain man was there, which had an infirmity thirty and eight years.

modern.text: One man there had been an invalid for thirty-eight years.

original.text: ἦν δέ τις ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖ ⸀τριάκοντα ὀκτὼ ἔτη ἔχων ἐν τῇ ἀσθενείᾳ ⸀αὐτοῦ·

verses.restored: Jesus, seeing this one lying there and knowing that he had already been so a long time, says to him, Do you want to become whole?

familiar.text: When Jesus saw him lie, and knew that he had been now a long time in that case, he saith unto him, Wilt thou be made whole?

modern.text: When Jesus saw him lying there and realized that he had spent a long time in this condition, He asked him, “Do you want to get well?”

original.text: τοῦτον ἰδὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς κατακείμενον, καὶ γνοὺς ὅτι πολὺν ἤδη χρόνον ἔχει, λέγει αὐτῷ· Θέλεις ὑγιὴς γενέσθαι;

verses.restored: The weakened one answered him, Lord, I have no human to put me into the pool when the water is stirred; while I am coming, another goes down before me.

familiar.text: The impotent man answered him, Sir, I have no man, when the water is troubled, to put me into the pool: but while I am coming, another steppeth down before me.

modern.text: “Sir,” the invalid replied, “I have no one to help me into the pool when the water is stirred. While I am on my way, someone else goes in before me.”

original.text: ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ ὁ ἀσθενῶν· Κύριε, ἄνθρωπον οὐκ ἔχω ἵνα ὅταν ταραχθῇ τὸ ὕδωρ βάλῃ με εἰς τὴν κολυμβήθραν· ἐν ᾧ δὲ ἔρχομαι ἐγὼ ἄλλος πρὸ ἐμοῦ καταβαίνει.

verses.restored: Jesus says to him, Rise, take up your mat, and walk.

familiar.text: Jesus saith unto him, Rise, take up thy bed, and walk.

modern.text: Then Jesus told him, “Get up, pick up your mat, and walk.”

original.text: λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· ⸀Ἔγειρε ἆρον τὸν κράβαττόν σου καὶ περιπάτει.

verses.restored: Immediately the human became whole, took up his mat, and walked. Now that day was Sabbath.

familiar.text: And immediately the man was made whole, and took up his bed, and walked: and on the same day was the sabbath.

modern.text: Immediately the man was made well, and he picked up his mat and began to walk. Now this happened on the Sabbath day,

original.text: καὶ εὐθέως ἐγένετο ὑγιὴς ὁ ἄνθρωπος καὶ ἦρε τὸν κράβαττον αὐτοῦ καὶ περιεπάτει. Ἦν δὲ σάββατον ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ.

verses.restored: Therefore the Judeans were saying to the one healed, It is Sabbath, and it is not lawful for you to carry the mat.

familiar.text: The Jews therefore said unto him that was cured, It is the sabbath day: it is not lawful for thee to carry thy bed.

modern.text: so the Jews said to the man who had been healed, “This is the Sabbath! It is unlawful for you to carry your mat.”

original.text: ἔλεγον οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι τῷ τεθεραπευμένῳ· Σάββατόν ἐστιν, ⸀καὶ οὐκ ἔξεστίν σοι ἆραι τὸν ⸀κράβαττον.

verses.restored: He answered them, The one who made me whole, that one said to me, Take up your mat and walk.

familiar.text: He answered them, He that made me whole, the same said unto me, Take up thy bed, and walk.

modern.text: But he answered, “The man who made me well told me, ‘Pick up your mat and walk.’”

original.text: ⸂ὃς δὲ⸃ ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς· Ὁ ποιήσας με ὑγιῆ ἐκεῖνός μοι εἶπεν Ἆρον τὸν κράβαττόν σου καὶ περιπάτει.

verses.restored: They asked him, Who is the human who said to you, Take up and walk?

familiar.text: Then asked they him, What man is that which said unto thee, Take up thy bed, and walk?

modern.text: “Who is this man who told you to pick it up and walk?” they asked.

original.text: ἠρώτησαν ⸀οὖν αὐτόν· Τίς ἐστιν ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὁ εἰπών σοι· ⸀Ἆρον καὶ περιπάτει;

verses.restored: The one healed did not know who it was, for Jesus had withdrawn, a crowd being in the place.

familiar.text: And he that was healed wist not who it was: for Jesus had conveyed himself away, a multitude being in that place.

modern.text: But the man who was healed did not know who it was, for Jesus had slipped away while the crowd was there.

original.text: ὁ δὲ ἰαθεὶς οὐκ ᾔδει τίς ἐστιν, ὁ γὰρ Ἰησοῦς ἐξένευσεν ὄχλου ὄντος ἐν τῷ τόπῳ.

verses.restored: After these things Jesus finds him in the temple and said to him, Look, you have become whole; do not continue in misalignment, so that something worse may not happen to you.

familiar.text: Afterward Jesus findeth him in the temple, and said unto him, Behold, thou art made whole: sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee.

modern.text: Afterward, Jesus found the man at the temple and said to him, “See, you have been made well. Stop sinning, or something worse may happen to you.”

original.text: μετὰ ταῦτα εὑρίσκει αὐτὸν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἴδε ὑγιὴς γέγονας· μηκέτι ἁμάρτανε, ἵνα μὴ χεῖρόν ⸂σοί τι⸃ γένηται.

verses.restored: The human went away and reported to the Judeans that Jesus was the one who made him whole.

familiar.text: The man departed, and told the Jews that it was Jesus, which had made him whole.

modern.text: And the man went away and told the Jews that it was Jesus who had made him well. The Father and the Son

original.text: ἀπῆλθεν ὁ ἄνθρωπος καὶ ⸀ἀνήγγειλεν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἐστιν ὁ ποιήσας αὐτὸν ὑγιῆ.

verses.restored: Because of this the Judeans were pursuing Jesus, because he was doing these things on Sabbath.

familiar.text: And therefore did the Jews persecute Jesus, and sought to slay him, because he had done these things on the sabbath day.

modern.text: Now because Jesus was doing these things on the Sabbath, the Jews began to persecute Him.

original.text: καὶ διὰ τοῦτο ἐδίωκον ⸂οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι τὸν Ἰησοῦν⸃ ὅτι ταῦτα ἐποίει ἐν σαββάτῳ.

verses.restored: But Jesus answered them, My Father is working until now, and I am working.

familiar.text: But Jesus answered them, My Father worketh hitherto, and I work.

modern.text: But Jesus answered them, “To this very day My Father is at His work, and I too am working.”

original.text: ὁ ⸀δὲ ἀπεκρίνατο αὐτοῖς· Ὁ πατήρ μου ἕως ἄρτι ἐργάζεται κἀγὼ ἐργάζομαι.

verses.restored: Because of this therefore the Judeans were seeking even more to kill him, because not only was he loosening the Sabbath, but he was also calling the Divine his own Father, making himself equal with the Divine.

familiar.text: Therefore the Jews sought the more to kill him, because he not only had broken the sabbath, but said also that God was his Father, making himself equal with God.

modern.text: Because of this, the Jews tried all the harder to kill Him. Not only was He breaking the Sabbath, but He was even calling God His own Father, making Himself equal with God.

original.text: διὰ τοῦτο οὖν μᾶλλον ἐζήτουν αὐτὸν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἀποκτεῖναι ὅτι οὐ μόνον ἔλυε τὸ σάββατον, ἀλλὰ καὶ πατέρα ἴδιον ἔλεγε τὸν θεόν, ἴσον ἑαυτὸν ποιῶν τῷ θεῷ.

verses.restored: Jesus answered and said to them, Amen, amen, I say to you: the Son is not able to do anything from himself except what he sees the Father doing; for whatever that One does, these things the Son likewise does.

familiar.text: Then answered Jesus and said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father do: for what things soever he doeth, these also doeth the Son likewise.

modern.text: So Jesus replied, “Truly, truly, I tell you, the Son can do nothing by Himself, unless He sees the Father doing it. For whatever the Father does, the Son also does.

original.text: Ἀπεκρίνατο οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ ⸀ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐ δύναται ὁ υἱὸς ποιεῖν ἀφʼ ἑαυτοῦ οὐδὲν ⸀ἐὰν μή τι βλέπῃ τὸν πατέρα ποιοῦντα· ἃ γὰρ ἂν ἐκεῖνος ποιῇ, ταῦτα καὶ ὁ υἱὸς ὁμοίως ποιεῖ.

verses.restored: For the Father loves the Son and shows him all things that he himself does; and greater works than these he will show him, so that you may marvel.

familiar.text: For the Father loveth the Son, and sheweth him all things that himself doeth: and he will shew him greater works than these, that ye may marvel.

modern.text: The Father loves the Son and shows Him all He does. And to your amazement, He will show Him even greater works than these.

original.text: ὁ γὰρ πατὴρ φιλεῖ τὸν υἱὸν καὶ πάντα δείκνυσιν αὐτῷ ἃ αὐτὸς ποιεῖ, καὶ μείζονα τούτων δείξει αὐτῷ ἔργα, ἵνα ὑμεῖς θαυμάζητε.

verses.restored: For just as the Father raises the dead and makes alive, so also the Son makes alive whom he wills.

familiar.text: For as the Father raiseth up the dead, and quickeneth them; even so the Son quickeneth whom he will.

modern.text: For just as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, so also the Son gives life to whom He wishes.

original.text: ὥσπερ γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ ἐγείρει τοὺς νεκροὺς καὶ ζῳοποιεῖ, οὕτως καὶ ὁ υἱὸς οὓς θέλει ζῳοποιεῖ.

verses.restored: For the Father judges no one, but has given all judgment to the Son,

familiar.text: For the Father judgeth no man, but hath committed all judgment unto the Son:

modern.text: Furthermore, the Father judges no one, but has assigned all judgment to the Son,

original.text: οὐδὲ γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ κρίνει οὐδένα, ἀλλὰ τὴν κρίσιν πᾶσαν δέδωκεν τῷ υἱῷ,

verses.restored: so that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father. The one not honoring the Son does not honor the Father who sent him.

familiar.text: That all men should honour the Son, even as they honour the Father. He that honoureth not the Son honoureth not the Father which hath sent him.

modern.text: so that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father. Whoever does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent Him.

original.text: ἵνα πάντες τιμῶσι τὸν υἱὸν καθὼς τιμῶσι τὸν πατέρα. ὁ μὴ τιμῶν τὸν υἱὸν οὐ τιμᾷ τὸν πατέρα τὸν πέμψαντα αὐτόν.

verses.restored: Amen, amen, I say to you: the one hearing my word and trusting the One who sent me has age-long life and does not come into judgment, but has crossed over from death into life.

familiar.text: Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life, and shall not come into condemnation; but is passed from death unto life.

modern.text: Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever hears My word and believes Him who sent Me has eternal life and will not come under judgment. Indeed, he has crossed over from death to life.

original.text: Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ὁ τὸν λόγον μου ἀκούων καὶ πιστεύων τῷ πέμψαντί με ἔχει ζωὴν αἰώνιον, καὶ εἰς κρίσιν οὐκ ἔρχεται ἀλλὰ μεταβέβηκεν ἐκ τοῦ θανάτου εἰς τὴν ζωήν.

verses.restored: Amen, amen, I say to you: an hour is coming and now is, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of the Divine, and those hearing will live.

familiar.text: Verily, verily, I say unto you, The hour is coming, and now is, when the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of God: and they that hear shall live.

modern.text: Truly, truly, I tell you, the hour is coming and has now come when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live.

original.text: Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἔρχεται ὥρα καὶ νῦν ἐστιν ὅτε οἱ νεκροὶ ⸀ἀκούσουσιν τῆς φωνῆς τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ οἱ ἀκούσαντες ⸀ζήσουσιν.

verses.restored: For just as the Father has life in himself, so he gave also to the Son to have life in himself.

familiar.text: For as the Father hath life in himself; so hath he given to the Son to have life in himself;

modern.text: For as the Father has life in Himself, so also He has granted the Son to have life in Himself.

original.text: ὥσπερ γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ ἔχει ζωὴν ἐν ἑαυτῷ, οὕτως ⸂καὶ τῷ υἱῷ ἔδωκεν⸃ ζωὴν ἔχειν ἐν ἑαυτῷ·

verses.restored: And he gave him authority to make judgment, because he is Son of Humanity.

familiar.text: And hath given him authority to execute judgment also, because he is the Son of man.

modern.text: And He has given Him authority to execute judgment, because He is the Son of Man.

original.text: καὶ ἐξουσίαν ἔδωκεν ⸀αὐτῷ κρίσιν ποιεῖν, ὅτι υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου ἐστίν.

verses.restored: Do not marvel at this, because an hour is coming in which all those in the tombs will hear his voice,

familiar.text: Marvel not at this: for the hour is coming, in the which all that are in the graves shall hear his voice,

modern.text: Do not be amazed at this, for the hour is coming when all who are in their graves will hear His voice

original.text: μὴ θαυμάζετε τοῦτο, ὅτι ἔρχεται ὥρα ἐν ᾗ πάντες οἱ ἐν τοῖς μνημείοις ⸀ἀκούσουσιν τῆς φωνῆς αὐτοῦ

verses.restored: and will come out: those doing good into resurrection of life, but those practicing harmful things into resurrection of judgment.

familiar.text: And shall come forth; they that have done good, unto the resurrection of life; and they that have done evil, unto the resurrection of damnation.

modern.text: and come out—those who have done good to the resurrection of life, and those who have done evil to the resurrection of judgment.

original.text: καὶ ἐκπορεύσονται οἱ τὰ ἀγαθὰ ποιήσαντες εἰς ἀνάστασιν ζωῆς, οἱ ⸀δὲ τὰ φαῦλα πράξαντες εἰς ἀνάστασιν κρίσεως.

verses.restored: I am not able to do anything from myself. As I hear, I judge; and my judgment is just, because I do not seek my own will but the will of the One who sent me.

familiar.text: I can of mine own self do nothing: as I hear, I judge: and my judgment is just; because I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me.

modern.text: I can do nothing by Myself; I judge only as I hear. And My judgment is just, because I do not seek My own will, but the will of Him who sent Me. Testimonies about Jesus

original.text: Οὐ δύναμαι ἐγὼ ποιεῖν ἀπʼ ἐμαυτοῦ οὐδέν· καθὼς ἀκούω κρίνω, καὶ ἡ κρίσις ἡ ἐμὴ δικαία ἐστίν, ὅτι οὐ ζητῶ τὸ θέλημα τὸ ἐμὸν ἀλλὰ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πέμψαντός ⸀με.

verses.restored: If I bear witness concerning myself, my witness is not true/valid by itself.

familiar.text: If I bear witness of myself, my witness is not true.

modern.text: If I testify about Myself, My testimony is not valid.

original.text: Ἐὰν ἐγὼ μαρτυρῶ περὶ ἐμαυτοῦ, ἡ μαρτυρία μου οὐκ ἔστιν ἀληθής·

verses.restored: There is another bearing witness concerning me, and I know that the witness he bears concerning me is true.

familiar.text: There is another that beareth witness of me; and I know that the witness which he witnesseth of me is true.

modern.text: There is another who testifies about Me, and I know that His testimony about Me is valid.

original.text: ἄλλος ἐστὶν ὁ μαρτυρῶν περὶ ἐμοῦ, καὶ οἶδα ὅτι ἀληθής ἐστιν ἡ μαρτυρία ἣν μαρτυρεῖ περὶ ἐμοῦ.

verses.restored: You have sent to John, and he has borne witness to the truth.

familiar.text: Ye sent unto John, and he bare witness unto the truth.

modern.text: You have sent to John, and he has testified to the truth.

original.text: ὑμεῖς ἀπεστάλκατε πρὸς Ἰωάννην, καὶ μεμαρτύρηκε τῇ ἀληθείᾳ·

verses.restored: But I do not receive witness from a human; rather I say these things so that you may be saved/healed.

familiar.text: But I receive not testimony from man: but these things I say, that ye might be saved.

modern.text: Even though I do not accept human testimony, I say these things so that you may be saved.

original.text: ἐγὼ δὲ οὐ παρὰ ἀνθρώπου τὴν μαρτυρίαν λαμβάνω, ἀλλὰ ταῦτα λέγω ἵνα ὑμεῖς σωθῆτε.

verses.restored: That one was the lamp burning and shining, and you were willing to rejoice for an hour in his light.

familiar.text: He was a burning and a shining light: and ye were willing for a season to rejoice in his light.

modern.text: John was a lamp that burned and gave light, and you were willing for a season to bask in his light.

original.text: ἐκεῖνος ἦν ὁ λύχνος ὁ καιόμενος καὶ φαίνων, ὑμεῖς δὲ ἠθελήσατε ἀγαλλιαθῆναι πρὸς ὥραν ἐν τῷ φωτὶ αὐτοῦ·

verses.restored: But I have the witness greater than John: the works the Father has given me to complete, these works that I do bear witness concerning me that the Father has sent me.

familiar.text: But I have greater witness than that of John: for the works which the Father hath given me to finish, the same works that I do, bear witness of me, that the Father hath sent me.

modern.text: But I have testimony more substantial than that of John. For the works that the Father has given Me to accomplish—the very works I am doing—testify about Me that the Father has sent Me.

original.text: ἐγὼ δὲ ἔχω τὴν μαρτυρίαν ⸀μείζω τοῦ Ἰωάννου, τὰ γὰρ ἔργα ἃ ⸀δέδωκέν μοι ὁ πατὴρ ἵνα τελειώσω αὐτά, αὐτὰ τὰ ἔργα ⸀ἃ ποιῶ, μαρτυρεῖ περὶ ἐμοῦ ὅτι ὁ πατήρ με ἀπέσταλκεν,

verses.restored: The Father who sent me has himself borne witness concerning me. You have neither heard his voice at any time nor seen his form,

familiar.text: And the Father himself, which hath sent me, hath borne witness of me. Ye have neither heard his voice at any time, nor seen his shape.

modern.text: And the Father who sent Me has Himself testified about Me. You have never heard His voice nor seen His form,

original.text: καὶ ὁ πέμψας με πατὴρ ⸀ἐκεῖνος μεμαρτύρηκεν περὶ ἐμοῦ. οὔτε φωνὴν αὐτοῦ ⸂πώποτε ἀκηκόατε⸃ οὔτε εἶδος αὐτοῦ ἑωράκατε,

verses.restored: and you do not have his word remaining in you, because the one whom he sent, this one you do not trust.

familiar.text: And ye have not his word abiding in you: for whom he hath sent, him ye believe not.

modern.text: nor does His word abide in you, because you do not believe the One He sent. The Witness of Scripture (Luke 16:19–31)

original.text: καὶ τὸν λόγον αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἔχετε ⸂ἐν ὑμῖν μένοντα⸃, ὅτι ὃν ἀπέστειλεν ἐκεῖνος τούτῳ ὑμεῖς οὐ πιστεύετε.

verses.restored: You search the Scriptures because you think in them to have age-long life; and those are the ones bearing witness concerning me.

familiar.text: Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me.

modern.text: You pore over the Scriptures because you presume that by them you possess eternal life. These are the very words that testify about Me,

original.text: Ἐραυνᾶτε τὰς γραφάς, ὅτι ὑμεῖς δοκεῖτε ἐν αὐταῖς ζωὴν αἰώνιον ἔχειν· καὶ ἐκεῖναί εἰσιν αἱ μαρτυροῦσαι περὶ ἐμοῦ·

verses.restored: Yet you are not willing to come to me so that you may have life.

familiar.text: And ye will not come to me, that ye might have life.

modern.text: yet you refuse to come to Me to have life.

original.text: καὶ οὐ θέλετε ἐλθεῖν πρός με ἵνα ζωὴν ἔχητε.

verses.restored: I do not receive glory from humans.

familiar.text: I receive not honour from men.

modern.text: I do not accept glory from men,

original.text: δόξαν παρὰ ἀνθρώπων οὐ λαμβάνω,

verses.restored: But I know you, that you do not have the love of the Divine in yourselves.

familiar.text: But I know you, that ye have not the love of God in you.

modern.text: but I know you, that you do not have the love of God within you.

original.text: ἀλλὰ ἔγνωκα ὑμᾶς ὅτι τὴν ἀγάπην τοῦ θεοῦ οὐκ ἔχετε ἐν ἑαυτοῖς.

verses.restored: I have come in my Father's name, and you do not receive me; if another comes in his own name, that one you will receive.

familiar.text: I am come in my Father’s name, and ye receive me not: if another shall come in his own name, him ye will receive.

modern.text: I have come in My Father’s name, and you have not received Me; but if someone else comes in his own name, you will receive him.

original.text: ἐγὼ ἐλήλυθα ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ πατρός μου καὶ οὐ λαμβάνετέ με· ἐὰν ἄλλος ἔλθῃ ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τῷ ἰδίῳ, ἐκεῖνον λήμψεσθε.

verses.restored: How are you able to trust, receiving glory from one another and not seeking the glory that is from the only Divine?

familiar.text: How can ye believe, which receive honour one of another, and seek not the honour that cometh from God only?

modern.text: How can you believe if you accept glory from one another, yet do not seek the glory that comes from the only God?

original.text: πῶς δύνασθε ὑμεῖς πιστεῦσαι, δόξαν παρʼ ἀλλήλων λαμβάνοντες, καὶ τὴν δόξαν τὴν παρὰ τοῦ μόνου θεοῦ οὐ ζητεῖτε;

verses.restored: Do not think that I will accuse you before the Father; the one accusing you is Moses, in whom you have hoped.

familiar.text: Do not think that I will accuse you to the Father: there is one that accuseth you, even Moses, in whom ye trust.

modern.text: Do not think that I will accuse you before the Father. Your accuser is Moses, in whom you have put your hope.

original.text: μὴ δοκεῖτε ὅτι ἐγὼ κατηγορήσω ὑμῶν πρὸς τὸν πατέρα· ἔστιν ὁ κατηγορῶν ὑμῶν Μωϋσῆς, εἰς ὃν ὑμεῖς ἠλπίκατε.

verses.restored: For if you trusted Moses, you would trust me, for that one wrote concerning me.

familiar.text: For had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me: for he wrote of me.

modern.text: If you had believed Moses, you would believe Me, because he wrote about Me.

original.text: εἰ γὰρ ἐπιστεύετε Μωϋσεῖ, ἐπιστεύετε ἂν ἐμοί, περὶ γὰρ ἐμοῦ ἐκεῖνος ἔγραψεν.

verses.restored: But if you do not trust his writings, how will you trust my words?

familiar.text: But if ye believe not his writings, how shall ye believe my words?

modern.text: But since you do not believe what he wrote, how will you believe what I say?”

original.text: εἰ δὲ τοῖς ἐκείνου γράμμασιν οὐ πιστεύετε, πῶς τοῖς ἐμοῖς ῥήμασιν πιστεύσετε;
